literal: Good resulting wealth great even if, to the noble ones, having killed resulting wealth lowest.
translation: Even if the resulting wealth is great and good, to the noble, wealth gained by killing is the lowest.
modern: நன்மையாக வரும் செல்வம் மிகப் பெரியதாக இருந்தாலும், ஓர் உயிரைக் கொன்று வரும் செல்வத்தைச் சான்றோர் மிகக் கீழானதாகவே கருதுவர்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the value of wealth with the means of acquiring it. The phrase 'நன்றாகும் ஆக்கம்' refers to wealth that is considered good or brings good. The poet states that no matter how vast and beneficial such prosperity might seem, if it is obtained through taking a life ('கொன்று ஆகும் ஆக்கம்'), it is deemed the absolute worst ('கடை') by noble people. The core message is that the end never justifies the means, especially when the means involves killing.
